candidates.alternative: A trusted distribution channel or checking the originating commit.
candidates.change: A signed verification bundle can carry provenance alongside delivery; no dated capability crossing is established.
candidates.obstruction: No signed bundle or trusted certificate identity supplied.
candidates.outcome: Bind received bytes to an independently trusted publisher.
candidates.route: Obtain publisher trust policy and verify the actual signed release.
candidates.scale: One verification per artifact plus identity-policy maintenance.
candidates.test: Attempt a legitimate signed/unsigned comparison using the exact receipt.
candidates.title: Verify release identity before opening
candidates.value: Could reduce the cost of false provenance; signing and review obligations remain.

candidates.alternative: GNU SHA-256 plus exact name-set comparison.
candidates.change: A pinned current publication defines the delivery set; byte comparison itself is established.
candidates.obstruction: The manifest must be trusted independently of delivered bytes.
candidates.outcome: Identify exact matches, omissions, changes and unexpected names.
candidates.route: Compile a closed local comparison from the declared names and digests.
candidates.scale: Deterministic across finite input bundles; larger datasets require resource testing.
candidates.test: Run a clean receipt and mixed defects without network or writes.
candidates.title: Build an offline two-file receipt checker
candidates.value: May eliminate manual file matching; price and reviewer time remain unmeasured.

candidates.change: The GNU release predates the investigation cutoff.
candidates.obstruction: Checksum listings alone do not establish the complete set of received names.
candidates.outcome: Obtain the requested four-way classification with familiar local tools.
candidates.route: Compare the inventory sets and hash their intersection with coreutils.
candidates.scale: One file scan per delivery; maintain an inventory wrapper.
candidates.test: Run unchanged and extra-name cases against the same frozen expectations.
candidates.title: Use an existing digest and inventory workflow
candidates.value: Avoid new runtime adoption where coreutils already operates.

candidates.alternative: The incumbent repository build and manual visual review.
candidates.change: The current release defines assets to exercise.
candidates.obstruction: A visual acceptance threshold and representative rendering environment were not provided.
candidates.outcome: Discover styling regressions the expected bytes themselves might contain.
candidates.route: Replay settled browser acceptance on a separately opened copy of the deliverable.
candidates.test: Inject a known visual regression and check the declared observable.
candidates.title: Verify the behavior of the received styles
candidates.value: Could catch failures that hashes preserve perfectly; browser operating costs remain.

candidates.alternative: Do nothing beyond the current release procedure.
candidates.change: Local diagnostics export might make collection easier but no reduction in drift is evidenced.
candidates.obstruction: No incident series or costs are supplied.
candidates.outcome: Determine how often delivery drift causes review or rework.
candidates.route: Preregister a private sample and collect consented, nonconfidential delivery outcomes.
candidates.scale: Observation per handoff; review labor remains.
candidates.test: Record one real discrepancy, its resolution and full review time.
candidates.title: Measure incident frequency before investing
candidates.value: Could justify reusing incumbent tools or staging further tooling.

candidates.alternative: A conventional local GNU verification wrapper with exactly the same observations.
candidates.beneficiary: Reviewer receiving an offline public MONTREAL.AI handoff
candidates.change: The project supplies a concrete release boundary to test. No AI crossing has been measured.
candidates.obstruction: Who controls the expected manifest determines what byte equality means; functional or publisher authenticity requires more evidence.
candidates.outcome: A portable receiver reports the exact four file classes under a separately pinned source reference.
candidates.route: Compile a manifest-specific local checker and run an independent GNU digest plus file-set reference on identical inputs.
candidates.scale: Each new bundle must supply fresh trusted names and digests; no cross-package inheritance of acceptance.
candidates.test: Try mixed changes, missing and extra names then malformed data and a bad name on both routes.
candidates.title: Bind the receipt to an out-of-band manifest and compare both verifiers
candidates.value: A recipient can inspect the file-level diagnosis without adopting release infrastructure. Additional value beyond existing tools needs measured handling and review costs.
